nindian-polity-75-4.s: Besides Kesavananda Bharati (1973), which case affirmed the Rule of Law as part of the Basic Structure?
o: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)
E.P. Royappa v. State of Tamil Nadu (1974)
Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975)
Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992)
nindian-polity-75-4.x: The Rule of Law was affirmed as a basic feature in Kesavananda Bharati (1973) and Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975).

ne8fe0d7294d.s: Carry-forward of backlog reserved vacancies is provided under Article:
ne8fe0d7294d.x: Article 16(4B) deals with backlog vacancies; 16(4A) concerns reservation in promotion for SCs and STs with consequential seniority.

nindian-society-45-8.s: Which case held that tribal land cannot be leased to private parties or corporations?
o: Janki Prasad Parimoo v. State of J&K
Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh
nindian-society-45-8.x: Samatha (1997) barred leasing tribal land to private parties or corporations; Janki Prasad Parimoo held caste alone cannot be the sole test of backwardness.

nindian-society-9-32.s: Which pair of clauses relates specifically to SCs, STs or OBCs?
nindian-society-9-32.x: Articles 15(4) and 16(4) concern SCs, STs or OBCs; Article 29 protects the cultural and educational rights of any section.

n97c9d2feb75.s: Which group lies outside the special provisions specifically described under Article 15?
n97c9d2feb75.x: Article 15 special provisions cover women, children, SEBCs, SCs, STs and, under 15(6), EWS; aged persons are not included.

nindian-society-9-7.s: The right of minorities to establish educational institutions is provided under Article:
nindian-society-9-7.x: Article 30 concerns minority educational institutions; Article 29 protects cultural and educational rights.

ne93284f7c99.s: Prescribing professional or technical qualifications for an occupation is permitted under Article:
ne93284f7c99.x: Article 19(6) allows general public interest, professional or technical qualifications and State trade or monopoly; Scheduled Tribes' protection belongs to 19(5).

n5430d94cb7c.s: There is no fundamental right under Article 19(1)(g) to carry on:
o: A lawful profession subject to reasonable regulation
A trade requiring prescribed technical qualifications
A dangerous or immoral trade such as trafficking
A lawful business subject to reasonable restrictions
n5430d94cb7c.x: No one has a right to carry on dangerous or immoral trades such as trafficking; lawful trades remain protected subject to reasonable restrictions.

nindian-polity-16-21.s: Without an Advisory Board's report, preventive detention under Article 22 cannot exceed:
nindian-polity-16-21.x: Article 22 limits preventive detention without an Advisory Board's report to three months.

nc4c990389b3.s: In which case was the ban on the journal Cross Roads struck down, as 'public order' was then not an Article 19(2) ground?
o: Romesh Thappar v State of Madras
Aveek Sarkar v State of West Bengal
Bennett Coleman v Union of India
Kedar Nath Singh v State of Bihar
nc4c990389b3.x: Romesh Thappar (1950) struck down the Cross Roads ban; it contributed to the First Amendment, 1951.

n2e17942bff1.s: An unlawful assembly of five or more persons, earlier under IPC Section 141, now falls under which section of the BNS?
n2e17942bff1.x: Unlawful assembly moved from IPC s.141 to BNS s.189; s.163 of the BNSS covers prohibitory orders.

ndbfd774e2e8.s: Which right is not expressly listed in Article 19(1) but has been read into freedom of speech and expression?
ndbfd774e2e8.x: Courts have read press freedom into Article 19(1)(a); there is no FR to strike, travel abroad is under Article 21 and 19(1)(f) was deleted.

n6c1e2eed010.s: Physical evidence such as fingerprints is not testimonial compulsion under Article 20(3), as held in:
n6c1e2eed010.x: Kathi Kalu Oghad (1961) held that fingerprints and physical specimens are not testimonial self-incrimination; Article 20(3) covers oral and documentary testimony.

nindian-polity-75-12.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Article 21?
o: Article 21 uses the expression 'procedure established by law'
A.K. Gopalan (1950) held a law valid if enacted through correct legislative procedure
After Maneka Gandhi (1978), a law must also be just, fair and reasonable
After Maneka Gandhi (1978), any procedure enacted by the legislature suffices
nindian-polity-75-12.x: Maneka Gandhi required the procedure to be just, fair and reasonable, so mere legislative enactment no longer suffices.

nindian-polity-75-16.s: An unguided and uncontrolled discretionary power conferred on an executive authority violates Article:
nindian-polity-75-16.x: Such discretion is arbitrary and subverts the Rule of Law, so it violates Article 14.

n6bbdb07222a.s: Emergency medical care was read into Article 21 in:
n6bbdb07222a.x: Paschim Banga Khet Mazdoor Samity concerned emergency medical care; Shafin Jahan is marriage by choice, Hoskot free legal aid, Hussainara speedy trial.

new.s: 'Descent' and 'residence' are barred grounds of discrimination under Article:
new.x: Article 16(2) adds descent and residence to the barred grounds; Article 15(1) lists only religion, race, caste, sex and place of birth.

new.s: Article 16 on equality of opportunity in public employment is available to:
new.x: Articles 15 and 16 are available to citizens only; Article 14 alone extends to all persons.

new.s: Article 16(4B) on carried-forward backlog vacancies was inserted by the:
new.x: The 81st Amendment (2000) inserted 16(4B), treating backlog vacancies as a separate group outside the 50% ceiling.

new.s: Consequential seniority for SC/ST promotions under Article 16(4A) was added by the:
new.x: The 77th Amendment (1995) gave promotion reservation; the 85th (2001) added consequential seniority, nullifying the catch-up rule.

new.s: Reservation in promotion for SCs and STs under Article 16(4A) was first provided by the:
new.x: The 77th Amendment (1995) inserted 16(4A) on SC/ST promotions, undoing Indra Sawhney on promotions.

new.s: Reservation in admissions under Article 15(5) does NOT apply to:
new.x: Article 15(5) covers admissions including private aided or unaided institutions but excludes Article 30 minority institutions.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the 103rd Constitutional Amendment:
1. It inserted Articles 15(6) and 16(6).
2. It was passed in the Lok Sabha as the 124th Amendment Bill.
3. It provides EWS reservation of up to 27%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The EWS quota is up to 10%; 27% is the OBC quota upheld in Indra Sawhney.

new.s: The National Commission for Backward Classes was given constitutional status under Article 338B by the:
new.x: The 102nd Amendment made the NCBC a constitutional body under Article 338B.

new.s: Economic equality in the Indian Constitution is mainly secured through:
new.x: Economic equality rests on DPSP Article 39(b), (c), (d) and is not part of the fundamental right to equality.

new.s: Political equality - no exclusion from electoral rolls and adult suffrage - is secured by Articles:
new.x: Articles 325 and 326 secure political equality; 39(b)-(d) secure economic equality and 17-18 social equality.

new.s: Articles 17 and 18 mainly secure which kind of equality?
o: Equality of opportunity in public employment
new.x: Articles 17 and 18 secure social equality (PYQ 2017); Article 18 does so by ending artificial distinctions.

new.s: 'Equal protection of the laws' under Article 14 is a:
new.x: Equal protection is American in origin and positive (like treated alike); equality before law is British and negative.

new.s: A.V. Dicey's 'Introduction to the Study of the Law of the Constitution', which set out the Rule of Law, was published in:
new.x: Dicey, a British jurist, expounded the Rule of Law in his 1885 book.

new.s: A system in which the ruler stays above the law and uses law as a weapon of state control is called:
new.x: Under Rule by Law the ruler is above the law; under Rule of Law the government is subordinate to law.

new.s: Article 14 permits reasonable classification but forbids:
o: Classification with a rational nexus to the object
Special provisions for women and children
new.x: Article 14 forbids class legislation, not reasonable classification based on intelligible differentia and rational nexus.

new.s: Immunity for a true, non-malicious report of proceedings of Parliament or State legislatures is given by Article:
new.x: Article 361A, inserted by the 44th Amendment (1978), protects true, non-malicious reports of legislative proceedings.

new.s: Immunity to MPs for anything said or any vote given in the House is provided by Article:
new.x: Article 105 gives MPs this immunity; Article 194 does the same for MLAs.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Article 361?
o: The President and Governors are not answerable to courts
No criminal case lies against a Governor during the term
A criminal case may be started against the President during the term after two months' notice
A civil case may be instituted only after two months' notice
new.x: Article 361 bars criminal cases during the term altogether; the two months' notice applies only to civil cases.

new.s: The Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955 was renamed by the 1976 amendment as the:
o: SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
new.x: The 1976 amendment renamed it the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, effective 19 November 1976.

new.s: The Protection of Civil Rights Act carries the year:
new.x: The renamed Act keeps the year 1955; 1976 is only the year of the amendment that renamed it.

new.s: The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act was enacted in:
new.x: The SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 is a further law against caste atrocities.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Article 17:
1. The term 'untouchability' is defined in the Constitution.
2. Enforcing any disability arising from untouchability is an offence punishable by law.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Only statement 2 is correct; 'untouchability' is not defined in the Constitution.

new.s: Under Article 18(2), an Indian citizen may accept a title from a foreign State:
new.x: Article 18(2) bars a citizen from accepting a foreign title at all; consent applies only under 18(3) and 18(4).

new.s: A non-citizen holding an office of profit or trust under the State needs whose consent to accept a foreign title?
new.x: Under Article 18(3), such a non-citizen needs the President's consent.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 18(3) – Non-citizen office-holder needs the President's consent for a foreign title
Article 18(1) – Citizen barred from accepting any foreign title
Article 18(2) – State confers no title except military or academic
Article 18(4) – Citizen may accept a foreign title with Parliament's consent
new.x: 18(3) is correctly matched; 18(1) bars State titles except military or academic, and 18(2) bars citizens from foreign titles.

new.s: Which case removed the requirement to prove backwardness of SCs and STs for reservation in promotion?
o: M. Nagaraj v. Union of India (2006)
Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992)
Jarnail Singh v. Lachhmi Narain Gupta (2018)
State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024)
new.x: Jarnail Singh (2018) removed the need to prove backwardness and extended the creamy layer to SC/ST promotions; Nagaraj had required quantifiable data.

new.s: The creamy layer exclusion and the 50% reservation ceiling originate in:
new.x: Both the creamy layer and the 50% cap originate in Indra Sawhney (1992).

new.s: Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022) upheld the EWS quota by a majority of:
new.x: Janhit Abhiyan upheld the 103rd Amendment by 3:2; Indra Sawhney was 6:3 and Davinder Singh 6:1.

new.s: Indra Sawhney (1992) was decided by a nine-judge bench by a majority of:
new.x: The Mandal case was decided 6:3 by nine judges.

new.s: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024), allowing sub-classification of SCs/STs, was decided by a majority of:
new.x: The seven-judge bench ruled 6:1 and overruled E.V. Chinnaiah (2004).

new.s: Which of the following pairs of case and holding is correctly matched?
o: Janki Prasad Parimoo – Upheld 10% EWS quota
Ashoka Kumar Thakur – Upheld the 93rd Amendment
new.x: Ashoka Kumar Thakur (2008) upheld the 93rd Amendment; Davinder Singh overruled E.V. Chinnaiah and the EWS quota was upheld in Janhit Abhiyan.

new.s: How many freedoms did Article 19(1) originally guarantee?
new.x: Article 19(1) had seven freedoms; deletion of 19(1)(f) left six.

new.s: The right to property under Article 19(1)(f) was deleted by the:
new.x: The 44th Amendment (1978) deleted 19(1)(f); the 97th added co-operative societies to 19(1)(c).

new.s: The Right to Freedom group in Part III comprises Articles:
new.x: The Right to Freedom group is Articles 19-22; Article 14 belongs to the Equality group.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the availability of Article 19:
1. A company, as a legal person, cannot claim Article 19.
2. Citizen shareholders of a company may sue for their Article 19 rights.
3. Kaushal Kishor (2023) held Articles 19 and 21 enforceable against non-State actors too.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are correct: Article 19 is for citizens only, not companies, though citizen shareholders may sue, and Kaushal Kishor extended enforcement to non-State actors.

new.s: Commercial speech was recognised as part of Article 19(1)(a) in:
new.x: Tata Press (1995) protected commercial speech; Naveen Jindal is flag hoisting and Bijoe Emmanuel the right to silence.

new.s: The right to information was read into freedom of speech in:
o: State of UP v. Raj Narain (1975)
new.x: Raj Narain (1975) read the right to know into 19(1)(a); PUCL concerned phone tapping.

new.s: Hoisting the National Flag, including on private buildings, was held part of freedom of expression in:
new.x: Naveen Jindal (2004) recognised hoisting the National Flag as part of 19(1)(a).

new.s: In which year was Sakal Papers, a press-freedom case, decided?
new.x: Sakal Papers was 1961; Kedar Nath (sedition) was 1962.

new.s: Which ground of restriction is found in Article 19(4) but NOT in Article 19(3)?
new.x: 19(4) allows sovereignty and integrity, public order and morality; 19(3) on assembly does not include morality.

new.s: Public order, friendly relations with foreign States and incitement to an offence were added to Article 19(2) by the:
new.x: The 1st Amendment (1951) added these grounds; the 16th (1963) added sovereignty and integrity.

new.s: Section 66A of the IT Act was struck down as vague and overbroad in:
new.x: Shreya Singhal (2015) struck down Section 66A of the IT Act.

new.s: In Bennett Coleman (1972), the Supreme Court held that press freedom was violated by:
o: A ban on the journal Cross Roads
A newsprint policy fixing the number of pages
new.x: Bennett Coleman struck down a newsprint policy fixing pages; Cross Roads was Romesh Thappar and 66A Shreya Singhal.

new.s: Kedar Nath Singh (1962) held sedition under Section 124A IPC valid only where there is:
new.x: Kedar Nath limited sedition to speech involving incitement to violence.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of case and ruling is correctly matched?
o: Anuradha Bhasin – Internet shutdowns must be proportionate, temporary and published
Shreya Singhal – Newsprint policy fixing pages struck down
Bennett Coleman – Section 66A of the IT Act struck down
Kedar Nath Singh – 'Community standards' test for obscenity
new.x: Anuradha Bhasin (2020) is correctly matched; the community standards test is from Aveek Sarkar (2014).

new.s: Which case held that government employees have no right to strike?
new.x: T.K. Rangarajan (2003) denied government employees a right to strike; CPI(M) v. Bharat Kumar held bandhs illegal.

new.s: Kameshwar Prasad (1962) held that:
o: A strike is a fundamental right
A demonstration is protected but a strike is not
A gherao is a peaceful assembly
new.x: Kameshwar Prasad protected demonstrations but not strikes; bandhs are illegal and gherao is not peaceful assembly.

new.s: Entry and settlement of outsiders in Inner Line areas may be limited to protect Scheduled Tribes under Article:
new.x: Under 19(5), movement and residence may be restricted to protect Scheduled Tribes' culture, land and property.

new.s: The freedom to move freely throughout the territory of India is guaranteed by Article:
new.x: 19(1)(d) covers movement; 19(1)(e) residence and settlement.

new.s: During a National Emergency, Article 358 suspends Article 19:
o: Only by a resolution of Parliament
Only after a Supreme Court order
new.x: Article 358 suspends Article 19 automatically; Article 359 needs a Presidential order.

new.s: After the 44th Amendment, Article 358 operates only for an emergency declared on the ground of:
o: Failure of constitutional machinery in a State
new.x: Since the 44th Amendment, Article 358 applies only to an emergency on war or external aggression, not armed rebellion.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Articles 358 and 359?
o: Articles 20 and 21 can be suspended under Article 359
Article 359 suspends only enforcement of the rights named
new.x: Since the 44th Amendment, Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended under Article 359.

new.s: Protection from torture is provided under Article:
new.x: Prohibition against torture is not in Article 20; protection from torture is under Article 21.

new.s: Article 20(1) bars retrospective application of:
new.x: Article 20(1) applies only to criminal laws, not to retrospective civil or tax laws.

new.s: Which case treated Articles 19, 21 and 22 as separate provisions?
new.x: Gopalan kept Articles 19, 21 and 22 separate; Maneka Gandhi linked 14, 19 and 21 as the golden triangle.

new.s: With respect to Article 21, capital punishment is:
new.x: Article 21 permits deprivation of life by a just, fair and reasonable procedure; capital punishment is not barred.

new.s: The right to livelihood was read into Article 21 in:
new.x: Olga Tellis (1985) recognised livelihood; Chameli Singh shelter, Subhash Kumar clean environment.

new.s: The right to marry a person of one's choice under Article 21 was upheld in:
o: Lata Singh v. State of UP (2006)
new.x: Lata Singh (2006), followed by Shafin Jahan (2018), upheld marriage by choice under Article 21.

new.s: The right to live with human dignity under Article 21 is associated with:
new.x: Francis Coralie Mullin (1981) read human dignity into Article 21; Hoskot is free legal aid.

new.s: The Puttaswamy (2017) judgment on privacy was delivered by a bench of:
new.x: A nine-judge bench unanimously (9:0) held privacy a fundamental right.

new.s: Puttaswamy (2017) overruled, to the extent they denied privacy as a fundamental right:
new.x: Puttaswamy overruled M.P. Sharma and Kharak Singh; Govind and Malak Singh had read privacy into Article 21.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the right to privacy:
1. It is protected mainly under Article 21.
2. Puttaswamy (2017) recognised it unanimously.
3. A limit on privacy must meet legality, legitimate aim and proportionality.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: All three are correct: privacy is under Article 21, Puttaswamy was 9:0, and its test is legality, legitimate aim and proportionality.

new.s: Which case declared Section 309 IPC (attempted suicide) unconstitutional?
new.x: P. Rathinam (1994) struck down Section 309; Gian Kaur (1996) overruled it and restored the section.

new.s: Passive euthanasia under High Court supervision was allowed in:
new.x: Aruna Shanbaug (2011) rejected the plea but allowed passive euthanasia under HC supervision; Common Cause upheld the living will.

new.s: After the 86th Amendment, Article 45 provides early childhood care and education for children:
new.x: Article 45 now covers children below 6; Article 21A covers 6 to 14.

new.s: Unnikrishnan v. State of AP (1993) held free education a right up to the age of:
new.x: Unnikrishnan held free education a right up to 14; beyond that it depends on the State's economic capacity.

new.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
A. Mohini Jain v. Karnataka
B. 86th Amendment
C. Unnikrishnan v. State of AP
D. RTE Act
new.x: Mohini Jain (1992), Unnikrishnan (1993), 86th Amendment (2002), RTE Act (2009).

new.s: Article 22(3) excludes from the safeguards of Articles 22(1) and 22(2):
o: Enemy aliens and persons under preventive detention
new.x: Article 22(3) excludes enemy aliens and preventive detainees.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT guaranteed to an arrested person under Article 22?
o: Being told the grounds of arrest
Production before the nearest magistrate within 24 hours
new.x: Article 22 does not guarantee bail as of right or trial by jury.

new.s: An arrested person must be produced before the nearest magistrate within:
new.x: Article 22(2) requires production within 24 hours, excluding journey time.

new.s: The Advisory Board under Article 22(4) consists of:
o: High Court judges or persons qualified to be such judges
new.x: The Advisory Board is made of HC judges or persons qualified to be HC judges.

new.s: COFEPOSA (1974) is mainly aimed at:
new.x: COFEPOSA targets smugglers and foreign-exchange manipulators; UAPA is the anti-terror law.

new.s: Under the National Security Act, a person may be detained without charges for up to:
new.x: The NSA (1980) allows detention up to 12 months without charges.

new.s: The first preventive detention law of independent India was the:
new.x: The Preventive Detention Act, 1950 was the first; it lapsed in 1969.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of law and year is correctly matched?
new.x: MISA was 1971; UAPA 1967, NSA 1980 and COFEPOSA 1974.

new.s: Since the 44th Amendment, the enforcement of which Articles can never be suspended under Article 359?
new.x: The 44th Amendment (1978) made Articles 20 and 21 non-suspendable even in a National Emergency.

new.s: Articles 20 and 21 were made non-suspendable during a National Emergency by the:
new.x: The 44th Amendment (1978) barred suspension of Articles 20 and 21 under Article 359; Puttaswamy reaffirmed this.
